title: Not classifying blues as gutsy or classic
summary: He says writers do not classify compositions; critics do.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: When you wrote your blues, di you prefer to write more in the gutsy or more in the classic blues?

Well, you see, they classify everything in the way they want to classify it. People classify it, classify this, classify that. They call them this. They call them that. All you do is just you write blues. That's the blues and then you don't classify that. I don't remember any writer that I know of classifying compositions.

You know, that's what I love about you. It's -- you just come right out and you lay it right on the line. And the funny thing. It's ironic. You know, it's just like in retrospect. People have to categorize --
-- you know. They have to pick something apart instead of letting it just live as it is.
